correctness.rationale: The statement uses all \(g\geq3\) and odd characteristic only. The established weight and containment formulas exhaust noncontained EO types in dimensions \(\lfloor g/2\rfloor+1\) and \(\lfloor g/2\rfloor+2\). For singleton support at indices \(h\) or \(h-1\), the distinguished cycle \(C_j\) (a singleton at \(j=1\), and \(C_j=(1,g,2,g-1,\ldots,j)\) for \(j\geq2\)) has exactly \(2j-2\) zero entries, one one entry and is unreachable from any good cycle; Muller Theorem 1.7 therefore gives emptiness. For support \(\{h,g\}\), the same underlying permutation has zero gaps of sizes \(1\) and \(2h-4\) between its two one entries; the unique nontrivial cycle is good, hence nonempty intersection. Known containment then establishes the mixed status. The standalone checker enumerated all increment vectors in genera three through fourteen and matched published counts; the infinite proof is symbolic and does not depend on enumeration.

originality.rationale: The exact all-genus first-two-dimension-layer classification, unique earliest disjoint type and unique earliest mixed type were not located in the relevant primary articles or indexed public findings. Görtz–Yu (2009/2012) already proves containment for \(\varphi_h=0\); Muller (2026) and Shimada (2026) give the strictly broader individual-type meeting tests. The boundary theorem is a new uniform evaluation requiring a weight partition and the three new explicit cyclic-parity comparisons. Shimada gives the position-two disjoint example, and Groen–Lupoian–Parker settle genus five; these special cases are openly recognized. Priority beyond inspected sources is not certified.
residual_risks: An overlooked equivalent all-genus boundary theorem in specialized older literature cannot be ruled out by finite bibliographic inspection.

value.rationale: The least possible dimensions of disjoint and partially intersecting EO strata are natural unknown sharp geometric thresholds in the Newton–EO intersection problem. The result identifies the unique exceptional type at each first layer and separates wholly supersingular, disjoint and genuinely mixed behavior. This all-genus structural phase boundary goes beyond genus-by-genus tables, arbitrary parameter slices or a mere restatement of the known pointwise decision procedure. Its geometric scope and characteristic restrictions are explicit.
